messages:
maria: heads-up — I just merged infra-modules@gpu-pool v1.4.0 into main (pinning instance types + kms alias change). CI plan passed but staging apply failed during terraform apply with immutable field errors.

maria: error snippet from the apply:
```
Error: Error updating aws_autoscaling_group.foo: InvalidParameterValue: Cannot change 'mixed_instances_policy' once set
   on modules/gpu-pool/main.tf line 92, in resource \"aws_autoscaling_group\" \"gpu_asg\":
```

maria: also saw kms alias replacement on aws_kms_key (plan shows Replace) — worried about decrypting existing disk snapshots.

sam-infra: thanks — can you paste the full plan for the asg change? did module v1.4.0 change the ASG to use mixed_instances_policy or change launch_template block?

maria: pasted plan to the PR, but here's the relevant diff:
```
~ resource aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_asg
    mixed_instances_policy {
      instances_distribution {
        on_demand_base_capacity = 0
      }
    }
~ launch_template {
+     launch_template_specification {
+       launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu_lt.id
+     }
  }
```

jen-ops: if ASG toggles between launch_template vs instance_type list terraform will want to replace. we probably need a migration path: create new ASG, drain & swap, then destroy old. can we do that in a controlled maintenance window?

oliver-ml: FYI model-training jobs in staging started failing immediately after the partial apply — nodes came up with fewer GPUs than expected (p3 -> p2 fallback). cost is also spiking because autoscaler reused on-demand.

kevin-sre: sounds like the module bump also pinned instance types and removed the previous override we used for gpu_count. that explains fallback. For KMS: replacing key will break access to AMI snapshot encryption if we don't re-encrypt or re-associate. We need to avoid Replace on the kms key.

kevin-sre: short-term mitigation: add lifecycle ignore_changes on aws_kms_key.alias or use aws_kms_alias resource to point to the new key without destroying. Example snippet:
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "redwood_job" {
  description = "Job encryption key"
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
resource "aws_kms_alias" "job_alias" {
  name          = "alias/redwood/jobs"
  target_key_id = aws_kms_key.redwood_job.key_id
}
# CI: avoid replacing key by not changing key material/rotation in the same PR
```

maria: good call. I can revert the kms alias change in the module and push a follow-up that does the ASG migration explicitly.

tfc-bot: workspace "infra-staging" run: apply failed in step "module.gpu-pool": Error: aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_asg (ID: asg-0abc123) – cannot modify mixed_instances_policy without replacement

sam-infra: let's do a staged approach — new module version v1.4.1 that adds a toggle var enable_mixed_instances = false by default. Then infra-staging can set enable_mixed_instances = true and we roll ASG creation via a canary ASG resource name. Once new ASG is healthy, update autoscaling group references and delete old.

jen-ops: agree. also add an upgrade note in the module CHANGELOG and a migration script (small terraform-runbook) with commands: 
```bash
# create new ASG
TF_VAR_enable_mixed_instances=true terraform apply -target=module.gpu-pool.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_asg_new
# cordon old nodes, drain, migrate jobs
# flip dns/instance group attachment
terraform apply -target=module.gpu-pool.update_refs
```

oliver-ml: for cost tracking, can we tag the new ASG with rollout=canary so cost-center reports don't get confused? otherwise finance will freak out.

maria: will include tags and a runbook. question: who will run the manual migration? I can do staging, but need someone from SRE for production window.

kevin-sre: I can take prod window next Wed 02:00 UTC. We'll also snapshot any encrypted EBS volumes before touching KMS. please add a preflight checklist to the PR.

maria: will open v1.4.1 PR with revert for KMS alias, enable_mixed_instances flag, and a migration.md in modules/gpu-pool/docs. tagging @sam-infra @kevin-sre @jen-ops.

deploy-bot: scheduled deployment for infra-modules/gpu-pool v1.4.1 to staging at 2024-04-02T01:00:00Z (manual apply required).

sam-infra: also: add a GitOps guard in the pipeline to fail fast if plan includes Replace on aws_kms_key or aws_launch_template. we've tripped that twice now. small policy check: if resources_to_replace contains "aws_kms_key" then fail unless EXEMPT_KMS=true.

maria: added a TODO in the PR to add policy, will follow up. thanks everyone.

kevin-sre: after this, can we add unit tests for module upgrades? i.e., a terratest that does v1.3 -> v1.4.1 upgrade in a short-lived env and asserts no unwanted replacements. would help catch regressions.

sam-infra: yes — add a github action that runs an upgrade plan and compares the plan JSON for replaces. parking this as infra-paydown ticket.

maria: closing the loop — PR created: https://github.com/redwood-infra/infra-modules/pull/712. ping on comments.
